$comment: Written reasons for the capabilities catalogue (docs/DSL_CAPABILITIES.html), batch 5 of N, 2026-11-23 (REG-357, owner: do only 20% of the remaining cases, of mixed complexity). One reason per keyword: what need it serves and why a lower rung of the extension ladder (expression, function, flow step, hand-written code) or an existing keyword cannot do it. The reasons state the need, not the evidence counts: the catalogue's own columns show samples, tests and examples and change as the corpus grows, so a count written here would go stale. The batch is every 5th keyword still without a reason, taken within each kind of value (boolean, text, number, choice, list, object, reference) so simple and complex ones are mixed. Key = slot id exactly as the catalogue shows it; the generator refuses a reason for a keyword the schema does not have.

reasons.agentAccessExposure.concept: To let a chat assistant look up customers, the app must say so; naming the concept offers its records as tools, so nothing is exposed that was not listed.
reasons.aggregateBalance.groupBy: Stock lines must balance per product and expiry date, not across the whole delivery; naming the grouping fields splits the collection into balance groups, and leaving it empty means one group for the whole collection.
reasons.aggregateCollection.childField: Order lines point back to their order through one field; naming it ties the child rows to the parent row so they load, save and delete together, which would be ambiguous if a child had more than one reference.
reasons.aggregateInvariant.name: When a rule over a whole order fails, the error the person sees must name the rule; the invariant's name is that identifier, required and unique inside the aggregate so two rules can never produce the same message.
reasons.autoPanel.selection: The list of rows on a generated screen, its columns, layout and tools, needs settings apart from the single-record view; a selection block holds them, so the list can differ without a hand-made page.
reasons.autoPanelSurface.derivedFields: A workbench showing an order draft should show the running total as the person edits, even though it is not stored; derived fields are display-only values recomputed from the current draft, so nothing extra is saved.
reasons.capability.specializes: A team that needs a payment capability almost like the one in a pack can start from that base and state only the difference, instead of copying it and losing track of where it came from.
reasons.capabilityAuth.roles: Only a finance role should call a payment capability; listing roles means a caller needs at least one of them, declared on the capability itself, where a check inside each flow could be forgotten.
reasons.capabilityPolicy.retryDelayMs: A flaky partner API often recovers after a short pause; waiting a set number of milliseconds between retries avoids hammering it, a behavior around the call that no flow step can provide from inside a single attempt.
reasons.cellGrid.layout: A seating plan fits a square grid, but a honeycomb shelf board looks right only with odd rows shifted half a cell; the layout choice changes how the board is drawn, a pure presentation matter.
reasons.cellGrid.valueField: On a seating plan, painting a cell with a palette entry stores the entry's id in one field of the cell row; valueField names it, and when it is a reference it must point at the palette query's concept so the stored id means something.
reasons.concept.lifecycle: An order moves through new, paid, shipped and delivered, and some jumps must be impossible; the lifecycle declares the status field, the states and the allowed transitions, so every screen, API and flow obeys one state machine instead of repeating the rule.
reasons.concept.specializesFloat: A team that copies a base concept from a shared pack normally wants the app frozen at the pack version it was built with, so an update cannot change it by surprise; this switch is for the team that prefers to follow the newest version, and it has to be declared because generation refuses once the pack has moved. No expression decides how a build resolves a pack.
reasons.conversion.from: When old data is converted, a new full-name field may be built from two old fields while another is only renamed; from names one field for copy, split, convert or case and two or more for merge or coalesce, so one keyword serves every conversion shape.
reasons.conversion.id: Each data conversion needs a stable name, because its generated hook lives in a folder named after it; the id is that name, unique among conversions.
reasons.documentBand.name: A printed invoice has bands such as header, lines and totals; each band needs a name, unique inside the document, so the layout can refer to it.
reasons.domainType.normalization: Emails typed with capitals and stray spaces should be stored the same way; naming normalizations such as trim and lowercase on the domain type cleans every field of that type before it is validated and stored, where cleaning inside flows would miss the screens and the imports.
reasons.event.uid: Renaming an event must not make the platform think the old one vanished and a new one appeared; a stable identity, generated once and never reused, lets a live element be matched to its model element even when the name differs.
reasons.field.minLength: A password or a tax code that is too short is always a mistake; stating the minimum on the field makes every screen, import and API refuse it, where a check written into each flow would miss the doors that do not run it.
reasons.field.properties: An address stored inside one field needs street, city and postcode, each with its own type; properties describe the inside of an object field as a map from property name to a schema, so the platform validates it, where a text field holding JSON would not.
reasons.flow.action: A button that starts a flow should say what it does, ask for confirmation when it is risky and look dangerous when it deletes; the action block holds the label, the confirmation and the danger level, so every screen presents the flow the same way.
reasons.flow.crossAggregateReason: The platform's rule is one aggregate in one transaction; a flow that must write two aggregates, such as a transfer between two accounts, may waive it for itself only, and the mandatory written reason makes the exception visible to the next reader.
reasons.flowInput.mode: A flow can be started with a request body that creates, updates, deletes or only queries; saying which one tells the platform what the caller must send and what the generated API accepts, which a step cannot say because it is settled before any step runs.
reasons.flowStep.condition: A refund over a limit goes to a manager; the condition is the expression a branch evaluates to choose then or else, so the decision is one readable line and not a step of its own.
reasons.flowStep.createIfMissing: An import that updates a customer by id should still work the first time that customer appears; this switch lets the update create the row, with a newly generated id, instead of failing with not found, where a read, a branch and a create would take three steps.
reasons.flowStep.onFailure: If charging a card works and booking the shipment then fails, the charge must be undone; compensation steps run in reverse order when a later step fails for good, as best-effort cleanup in the saga style and not a distributed transaction, and a plain step list cannot say that because they run only on failure.
reasons.flowStep.query: A step that needs the open tickets of a customer should reuse a declared query instead of describing the filter again; naming the query lets a runQuery step run it and bind the result to the step's output.
reasons.guidePageTheme.accent: A help page for one department may carry that department's color; an accent color changes the highlight across the page at once, a presentation choice only.
reasons.humanTask.record: An inbox task to approve a purchase should link to that purchase; naming the flow-state reference of the record, which must carry an id, gives the inbox the link.
reasons.inboundDoor.fieldMapping: A payment provider posts its own JSON with its own names for things; the mapping says which part of that body becomes which event field, so the app's events keep its own vocabulary, and when it is absent the raw body becomes the payload unchanged.
reasons.lifecycleState.label: The state code PAID_PARTIAL should read as Partly paid for people; the label is the text shown for the state, so the wording is chosen once for every screen.
reasons.lifecycleTransition.event: Moving an order to shipped should tell the rest of the system; naming the event that triggers the transition, and is published by it, lets flows and listeners react without polling the state.
reasons.lifecycleTransition.requiredPayload: An order cannot be shipped without a tracking number; naming the fields that must hold a value stops the transition otherwise, and the rule sits on the transition instead of being repeated in every screen and flow that ships orders.
reasons.pack:propertyScopes: A pack for multi-branch shops may need a scope such as branch for its settings; contributing property scopes lets the pack bring that structure along, where the app consuming it would have to declare the scopes again.
reasons.packRef.$ref: An app that keeps a pack's file next to the model points at it by relative path; it is the local alternative to a remote coordinate, and the two are mutually exclusive.
reasons.panelAction.procedure: A screen button must say which logic it runs; for a procedure binding the name is the flow of that name, so a screen action and a flow stay connected by one name.
reasons.panelAction.scope: A Refund button may sit once on the whole page for a bulk action, or once on every row for that row's refund; scope says which, and a row-scoped action is invoked with that row's id, which is what it needs to act on the right row.
reasons.panelFieldBinding.editable: A screen may show a field the person can read but not change, or one they can; this switch says which, per screen, without changing the concept, where the field's own rules would lock it everywhere.
reasons.panelFieldBinding.source: A panel with several data sources must know which one feeds a field; naming the source makes it explicit, and it defaults to the panel's primary source so the common case needs nothing.
reasons.panelLayout.metadata: A person who arranged a panel wants to leave a note for whoever comes next; free-form metadata carried into the compiled model untouched is that notebook, where a comment in the JSON would be lost on compile.
reasons.panelLayout.slots: A generated panel sometimes needs one hand-made region, such as a map or a chart, without replacing the whole screen; slots mount an app-owned component above, below or in place of the generated body, the door to hand-written code that the language deliberately leaves open.
reasons.presentationMetadata.defaultSort: A list of orders should open with the newest first; naming the field the list sorts by default says so once for the concept, instead of every screen setting its own.
reasons.presentationMetadata.formColumns: A concept with twenty fields makes a long create form; setting the number of columns lays it out in two or three, a presentation choice made once for the concept.
reasons.presentationMetadata.widget: A text field might be better as a text area, a select or a date picker; naming the control chooses how the field is edited, and the validator checks that it fits the field's type, which a style written as free text would not.
reasons.queryLookup.field: A report showing the average price of a product's offers must know which field of the lookup concept to average; field names it for every function except count, which counts rows.
reasons.referenceDefinition.onDelete: Deleting a customer who still has orders must either be refused, take the orders with it, or leave them with no customer; the choice on the reference says which, and it holds for every door that can delete, where a check in one flow would miss the others.
reasons.referenceDefinition.searchFields: Typing a customer's phone number into a picker should find them even if the picker shows names; naming the target fields the picker searches makes the search match what people actually type.
reasons.regionMount.component: A hand-made component such as a map is registered in the app's own web/regions folder; the component name says which one a region mounts, and it is required when the region renders a component, so the generated page can find it.
reasons.root:packs: An app that wants ready-made parts, such as a leave-request pack, must say which packs it uses and where each one comes from, a local file or a remote coordinate; the list is the model's dependencies, and no expression can pull a part in.
reasons.schemaObject.default: A data shape may want a missing value to become a known literal, such as standard shipping; the default is that literal, written once in the shape instead of in every caller.
reasons.seed.count: A demo needs two hundred sample customers, not two hundred lines of JSON; count says how many copies of the data to generate, the shorthand for when no index variables are needed.
reasons.transactionDerivedField.expression: A draft order's total should update as the person types, in the browser, with no round trip; for the client tier the expression is evaluated over the draft there, the expression language doing the work and this keyword being the place where it is asked.
reasons.transactionDerivedField.label: A derived total in a draft needs a caption such as Order total; the label is that caption, shown to people, with no logic behind it.
reasons.workbenchAction.visibleWhen: A Ship button should appear only for orders of one type; a client-side predicate over the root row shows the action only while it is true, evaluated in the browser so the button follows the person's edits at once.
reasons.workbenchBandPicker.columns: A picker of products is easier with code, name and price side by side; naming the columns says what the person sees when choosing, a presentation choice with no lower rung.
reasons.workbenchBandPicker.multiSelect: Adding five products to an order is faster if they can be ticked together; the switch lets the picker take several rows at once instead of one per round trip, and picker behavior is screen plumbing that no flow can change.
